articles_and_episodes.title: ALIA BLAND & CLAIRE DEEKS: Founders Of RCR & Voices For Freedom: Did Billionaires Really Shape the Election?
ALIA BLAND & CLAIRE DEEKS: RCR Co-Founders: Explaining RCR’s Election Strategy with Michael Laws
MAURICE WILLIAMSON: Former NZ MP & Statistician: Strategic Voting Delivers a Seismic Shift in the Election
DON BRASH & RODNEY HIDE: Former ACT Party Leader & Former Reserve Bank Governor: Election Debrief
NICOLE MCKEE: ACT Deputy Leader: ‘National Must Learn to Share Power’

youtube.title: ALIA BLAND & CLAIRE DEEKS
youtube.summary: Joining Paul Brennan, Claire Deeks and Alia Bland reflect on the Vote Smart 2026 campaign, explaining how RCR and Voices for Freedom conceived, organised and delivered a major grassroots-led strategic voting campaign – rather than the billionaire-driven operation portrayed in parts of the mainstream media. They discuss the campaign’s planning, electoral rules, media backlash and the controversy surrounding the overhang strategy. Check out the Vote Smart campaign For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday

youtube.title: 🇦🇺 Ardern is Heading to Australia to Teach Empathy. Seriously.
youtube.summary: 🇦🇺 Ardern is Heading to Australia to Teach Empathy. Seriously. Jacinda Ardern has a new role at the University of Sydney, focusing on empathetic leadership, social cohesion and civic trust. But as Michael Arbon asks, how can you teach trust without first acknowledging the damage left behind? #RCRMedia

youtube.title: DON BRASH & RODNEY HIDE
youtube.summary: Rodney Hide and Don Brash join Maree Buscke for a post-election discussion examining how vote-splitting has reshaped Parliament and whether special votes will determine the centre-right’s ability to govern alone. They also consider Christopher Luxon’s campaign performance, National’s relationship with ACT and NZ First, the potential influence of the Opportunity Party, and the challenges ahead in coalition negotiations. For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday

youtube.title: ALIA BLAND & CLAIRE DEEKS
youtube.summary: RCR and VFF co-founders Alia Bland and Claire Deeks explain to Michael Laws on The Platform how they developed and funded the Vote Smart 2026 campaign, designed to prevent a left-wing government while strengthening ACT and NZ First within a centre-right coalition. For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday

youtube.title: MAURICE WILLIAMSON
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke is joined by former NZ MP and Statistician Maurice Williamson to examine new analysis suggesting strategic voting and vote-splitting had a far greater impact on the election than previously seen, with more than 300,000 National electorate voters estimated to have chosen a different party for their party vote. They explore the electorate-by-electorate figures, the likely impact of special votes on the final result and the growing acceptance of split voting under MMP. For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday

youtube.title: LACHLAN LADE
youtube.summary: Chatting with Tim Wilms, Lachlan Laid from the Australia Lobby Group discusses the growing disconnect in Australian society, arguing that shared national values, identity and allegiance to the Australian flag have been eroded. He criticises both major political parties, outlines the Australia Lobby Group’s push for major immigration restrictions and explains its campaign to mobilise Australians and hold politicians accountable for restoring national identity. #RCR

youtube.title: NICOLE MCKEE
youtube.summary: ACT Deputy Leader Nicole McKee joins Maree Muscke for this post-election interview examining ACT’s record result of 13 MPs and its ambitions for a stronger coalition agreement. Nicole discusses the party’s increased negotiating influence, strategic voting and the debate over MMP, while calling on National to show greater respect for its coalition partners and recognise ACT’s contribution to the government’s achievements. Discover more on Nicole McKee or find her on Facebook For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday

youtube.title: GREG BARNS
youtube.summary: Barrister and civil liberties advocate Greg Barns SC joins Michael Arbon to discuss the proposed Digital Duty of Care bill and its potential consequences for free speech, privacy and government surveillance. They also explore Australia’s under-16 social media ban, the use of government sock-puppet identities and the upcoming Victorian election, including the state’s debt, crime policies and lack of commitment to civil liberties. Discover more from Greg at Lawyers Alliance or find him on X Find more from Michael on Facebook and X

youtube.title: MICHAEL ARBON
youtube.summary: Michael Arbon examines Dame Jacinda Ardern’s new role at the University of Sydney, where she will focus on empathetic leadership, social cohesion and civic trust, despite leaving New Zealand a divided nation. Discover more from Michael on Facebook and X

youtube.title: LISA SPENCER
youtube.summary: Comedian and Satirist Lisa Spencer shares her impressions of the Australia marches in Melbourne, describing a noticeably different energy and atmosphere from previous protests. She and Tim Wilms discuss the approaching Victorian election, their opposition to another Labor government and their hopes for political change in the state. #RCR

youtube.title: EDWARD SCHULLER
youtube.summary: Talking with Tim Wilms, Edward Schuller discusses efforts to challenge the influence of external organisations in school sex education, transgender ideology and what he describes as the growing bureaucratisation of education. Through the Protect Our Kids campaign, he is calling for these organisations to be removed from schools, their government funding cut and greater parental oversight restored. #RCR

youtube.title: MICHAEL PIASTRINO
youtube.summary: Talking with Tim Wilms One Nation candidate Michael Piastrino explains why he left the Liberal Party, accusing it of lacking backbone and failing to represent voters. He outlines One Nation’s ambitions to win seats across Melbourne’s south-east, promising to put local concerns first, including reversing the renaming of Berwick Springs Lake. #RCR

youtube.title: MARK NICHOLSON
youtube.summary: Speaking with Tim Wilms, cartoonist and One Nation candidate Mark Nicholson reflects on the energy behind the party’s growing election campaign and his decision to stand in Melbourne’s Northern Metropolitan Region. He discusses continuing his political cartoons if elected and argues that One Nation is now offering practical solutions, pointing to its 63-page policy platform. #RCR

youtube.title: RCR co-founders Alia Bland and Claire Deeks spoke to Michael Laws
youtube.summary: RCR co-founders Alia Bland and Claire Deeks spoke to Michael Laws this morning about RCR’s Vote Smart 2026 campaign.

youtube.title: UNDER THE HOOD
youtube.summary: Following his recent New Zealand tour, Graham “Hoody” Hood reflects on the political divisions he encountered, the growing tensions around the world and the need for people who value freedom to put their differences aside. With New Zealand’s election now behind us, Hoody delivers a timely message about rejecting hostility, finding common ground and building strong communities. Because we may not agree on everything, but we need to be able to stand together.
